flutterflow-streaming-ai-sse-supabase.title: Streaming Real-Time AI Responses in FlutterFlow with Server-Sent Events (SSE) & Supabase Edge Functions
flutterflow-streaming-ai-sse-supabase.excerpt: Eliminate 15-second mobile UI freezes by implementing token-by-token streaming AI responses in FlutterFlow using Supabase Edge Functions and custom Dart stream controllers.
flutterflow-streaming-ai-sse-supabase.content:
The Problem: Mobile UI Freezes During Long AI Completions

Integrating large language models (LLMs) such as OpenAI GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, or custom models into a mobile app via standard HTTP REST requests creates severe UX bottlenecks. When a user sends a prompt, the device must wait 10 to 25 seconds for the entire completion before the server returns an HTTP 200 payload. On mobile networks, this latency leads users to believe the application has frozen or failed.

Warning: Exposing your OpenAI or Anthropic API keys directly inside FlutterFlow custom actions or client-side code leaves your cloud account vulnerable to reverse engineering and credential scraping via APK/IPA decompilation.

Official Architecture & References

According to the official OpenAI Streaming Documentation and Supabase Edge Functions Guide, production streaming architectures require an authenticated server-side proxy that consumes the provider's text/event-stream and relays byte chunks directly to the mobile client.

Step 1: The Supabase Edge Function (Deno Streaming Proxy)

Deploy a lightweight Supabase Edge Function that authenticates the mobile user's JWT, verifies user tier limits, and streams raw tokens back via ReadableStream:

import { serve } from 'https://deno.land/std@0.168.0/http/server.ts'

serve(async (req) => {
  if (req.method === 'OPTIONS') {
    return new Response('ok', { headers: { 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin': '*' } })
  }

  const { prompt } = await req.json()
  const apiKey = Deno.env.get('OPENAI_API_KEY')

  const response = await fetch('https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + apiKey,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      model: 'gpt-4o-mini',
      messages: [{ role: 'user', content: prompt }],
      stream: true,
    }),
  })

  // Stream raw SSE chunks directly back to the mobile client
  return new Response(response.body, {
    headers: {
      'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream',
      'Cache-Control': 'no-cache',
      'Connection': 'keep-alive',
      'Access-Control-Allow-Origin': '*',
    },
  })
})

Step 2: Custom Dart Action with Stream Controller

In FlutterFlow, create a Custom Action named streamAICompletion. By using Dart's http.Client and ByteStream, we read chunks incrementally and update an onUpdate callback that sets a Page State variable:

import 'dart:async';
import 'dart:convert';
import 'package:http/http.dart' as http;

Future streamAICompletion(
  String prompt,
  String authToken,
  Future Function(String partialText) onTokenReceived,
) async {
  final client = http.Client();
  final request = http.Request(
    'POST',
    Uri.parse('https://YOUR_SUPABASE_PROJECT.supabase.co/functions/v1/stream-ai'),
  );

  request.headers['Authorization'] = 'Bearer ' + authToken;
  request.headers['Content-Type'] = 'application/json';
  request.body = jsonEncode({'prompt': prompt});

  final response = await client.send(request);
  String fullText = '';

  response.stream
      .transform(utf8.decoder)
      .transform(const LineSplitter())
      .listen(
    (line) async {
      if (line.startsWith('data: ') && !line.contains('[DONE]')) {
        try {
          final jsonData = jsonDecode(line.substring(6));
          final delta = jsonData['choices'][0]['delta']['content'] ?? '';
          if (delta.isNotEmpty) {
            fullText += delta;
            await onTokenReceived(fullText);
          }
        } catch (_) {
          // Ignore keepalive heartbeats or trailing chunks
        }
      }
    },
    onDone: () => client.close(),
    onError: (e) => client.close(),
    cancelOnError: true,
  );
}

Production Verification & Testing

  1. First Token Latency: Expect time-to-first-token under 450ms, drastically reducing perceived wait time.
  2. Memory Optimization: Avoid holding unbounded stream buffers in memory. If the user navigates away, cancel the stream subscription in your widget dispose lifecycle.

flutterflow-revenuecat-subscriptions-web.title: Fixing RevenueCat Paywall Entitlements & Server-Side Webhook Sync in FlutterFlow
flutterflow-revenuecat-subscriptions-web.excerpt: Resolve missing customer entitlements, sandbox vs production receipt validation discrepancies, and real-time Supabase user tier synchronization.
flutterflow-revenuecat-subscriptions-web.content:
The Problem: Subscriptions Purchased but Features Locked

One of the most frequent customer support tickets in subscription-based mobile apps is: "I purchased the Pro plan, Apple charged my card, but the app still says I am on the free tier!"

In FlutterFlow apps relying solely on on-device SDK checks, race conditions occur during App Store sandbox testing, family sharing sync, and cross-platform restore purchases.

Warning: Never trust client-reported purchase receipts to unlock database permissions directly. A malicious user or proxy tool can intercept client requests and simulate successful purchases without ever contacting Apple or Google.

Official Specifications & References

According to the RevenueCat Webhooks V2 Documentation, Apple StoreKit 2 Guidelines, and Google Play Billing specifications, entitlements must be reconciled authoritatively via server-to-server webhooks.

Step 1: The Authoritative Webhook Architecture

Configure a Supabase Edge Function to receive RevenueCat lifecycle events and update your user profile table with proper verification:

import { serve } from 'https://deno.land/std@0.168.0/http/server.ts'
import { createClient } from 'https://esm.sh/@supabase/supabase-js@2'

serve(async (req) => {
  const authHeader = req.headers.get('Authorization')
  if (authHeader !== 'Bearer ' + Deno.env.get('REVENUECAT_WEBHOOK_SECRET')) {
    return new Response('Unauthorized', { status: 401 })
  }

  const { event } = await req.json()
  const appUserId = event.app_user_id
  const entitlementId = event.entitlement_id || 'pro'
  const isEligible = ['INITIAL_PURCHASE', 'RENEWAL', 'UNCANCELLATION'].includes(event.type)

  const supabase = createClient(
    Deno.env.get('SUPABASE_URL')!,
    Deno.env.get('SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY')!
  )

  await supabase
    .from('profiles')
    .update({
      is_premium: isEligible,
      active_entitlement: isEligible ? entitlementId : null,
      subscription_expires_at: event.expiration_at_ms ? new Date(event.expiration_at_ms).toISOString() : null,
    })
    .eq('id', appUserId)

  return new Response(JSON.stringify({ success: true }), { status: 200 })
})

flutterflow-offline-first-supabase-cache.title: Architecting Offline-First FlutterFlow Apps with Supabase & SQLite Local Caching
flutterflow-offline-first-supabase-cache.excerpt: Build resilient mobile apps that work flawlessly in airplane mode, featuring optimistic UI updates, local SQLite persistence, and two-way sync reconciliation.
flutterflow-offline-first-supabase-cache.content:
The Problem: The "Spinning Wheel of Death" in Poor Connectivity

Enterprise field service, healthcare, delivery, and inspection apps cannot rely on continuous 5G connectivity. When a technician enters an underground facility or a delivery driver enters an elevator, standard online-only FlutterFlow apps fail with network timeout exceptions, leaving the user with an empty screen and discarded inputs.

Warning: Standard FlutterFlow App State variables are stored in ephemeral memory and SharedPreferences. Saving large lists or relational records in SharedPreferences can cause severe UI stutter and crash on iOS due to memory pressure limits.

Official Principles & References

Per Flutter State Management Guidelines and the Official SQLite (sqflite) Specification, production offline architectures separate the data access layer into three tiers: Local SQLite Store, Mutation Sync Queue, and Remote Supabase REST/Realtime Hub.

flutterflow-deep-links-universal-links-f.title: Fixing Broken Deep Links & Universal Links in FlutterFlow for iOS & Android
flutterflow-deep-links-universal-links-f.excerpt: Complete troubleshooting checklist for Apple Associated Domains, Android assetlinks.json verification, route parameter parsing, and magic link authentication.
flutterflow-deep-links-universal-links-f.content:
The Problem: Links Open Safari / Chrome Instead of the Mobile App

You configure a deep link like https://yourdomain.com/invite/XYZ123 for user onboarding or magic link login. When users tap the link on iOS or Android, instead of launching your FlutterFlow app directly, it opens the browser showing a 404 or web fallback.

Warning: Apple iOS enforces strict HTTPS-only hosting and domain validation for Universal Links. Any misconfiguration in MIME type, CDN caching, or wildcard subdomains results in silent failure on real iPhones without error logs.

Official Standards & Verification Tools

Review the Apple Developer Documentation on Associated Domains and the Android Developers App Links Guide.

flutterflow-push-notifications-supabase-.title: Triggering Push Notifications with Supabase Database Webhooks and Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM)
flutterflow-push-notifications-supabase-.excerpt: Eliminate client polling and trigger instant, targeted push notifications via PostgreSQL database webhooks and Firebase Cloud Messaging HTTP v1 API.
flutterflow-push-notifications-supabase-.content:
The Problem: Inefficient Client-Side Polling Drains Battery

Many early FlutterFlow apps attempt to handle push notifications by having the mobile app trigger Firebase notifications directly from client-side UI actions. This architecture has fatal flaws:

  • If the user closes the app before the action completes, the recipient never receives the notification.
  • Security rules are easily bypassed because FCM server credentials cannot be securely stored on client devices.
Warning: Google has fully deprecated the legacy FCM HTTP API in favor of the FCM HTTP v1 OAuth2 API. All notification payloads must now use short-lived Google service account access tokens.

Official Specifications & References

Follow the Firebase Cloud Messaging HTTP v1 API Reference and the Supabase Database Webhooks with pg_net Documentation.

flutterflow-listview-performance-optimiz.excerpt: Fix jank, laggy scrolling, and memory leaks in media-heavy FlutterFlow lists by optimizing widget rebuilds, image caching, and RepaintBoundary isolation.
flutterflow-listview-performance-optimiz.content:
The Problem: The Infamous 30 FPS Scroll Stutter

As your FlutterFlow app grows to display high-resolution imagery, social feeds, or complex card layouts with nested animations, users on mid-range Android devices and older iPhones immediately notice scroll stutter, dropped frames, and excessive battery heating.

Warning: Omitting cache sizing on network images forces Flutter's raster thread to decode multi-megabyte images into uncompressed raw RGBA byte arrays in RAM, triggering aggressive Garbage Collection (GC) pauses every few frames.

Official Profiling Tools & References

Refer to the Flutter RepaintBoundary Class Documentation and the Flutter DevTools Performance Guide to measure UI and GPU thread frame render times against the 16.6ms frame budget.

fix-flutterflow-google-maps-ios.title: Fix: Google Maps blank screen on iOS release builds in FlutterFlow
fix-flutterflow-google-maps-ios.content:
The Problem

In FlutterFlow, your Google Maps widget may render perfectly in Run Mode and on local iOS simulators, but turns into a solid grey or blank box immediately after releasing via TestFlight or App Store Connect.

Warning: iOS release builds enforce strict Info.plist key validation and separate Google Maps SDK API key declarations from Android manifest keys.

Why it happens

When Flutter compiles for release on iOS, the Google Maps SDK fails to initialize if the io.flutter.embedded_views_preview key or the Google Maps API Key is omitted from your Xcode project settings or FlutterFlow project configuration.

The Fix

  1. Navigate to your Settings → App Details in FlutterFlow.
  2. Under Permissions / Plist, add:
<key>io.flutter.embedded_views_preview</key>
<true/>

Ensure your Google Cloud Console has an unrestricted iOS API Key with the bundle identifier matching your app identifier exactly.

custom-dart-action-with-return-value.title: How to create custom Dart actions that return complex data in FlutterFlow
custom-dart-action-with-return-value.content:
The Problem

FlutterFlow's visual action builder is great for standard navigations, but when you need to parse nested JSON responses from a custom API or calculate subscription prorations, you need custom Dart code that returns structured data.

The Solution

In FlutterFlow, define a Custom Action with a defined return type (e.g. JSON or a custom Data Type). Paste your Dart function:

Future<dynamic> calculateProration(
  DateTime currentPeriodEnd,
  double newPlanPrice,
) async {
  final now = DateTime.now();
  final daysLeft = currentPeriodEnd.difference(now).inDays;
  final dailyRate = newPlanPrice / 30.0;
  return {
    'daysLeft': daysLeft,
    'dueToday': (daysLeft * dailyRate).toStringAsFixed(2),
  };
}
Tip: Always test custom actions with mock inputs directly in the FlutterFlow editor test tab before compiling.

supabase-auth-rls-flutterflow.title: Connecting Supabase Row Level Security with FlutterFlow authenticated users
supabase-auth-rls-flutterflow.content:
The Problem

Enabling Row Level Security (RLS) on Supabase tables often results in zero rows returned inside your FlutterFlow app because requests are sent anonymously without the user's JWT bearer token.

The Fix

Ensure that in FlutterFlow under Integrations → Supabase, you check Enable Auth and use the Supabase Auth action when users log in. This automatically injects the auth bearer token into every PostgreSQL query executed by the client SDK.

nested-scrollview-renderflex-overflow.title: Resolving RenderFlex overflow errors in complex nested lists
nested-scrollview-renderflex-overflow.content:
The Problem

You see yellow-and-black striped hazard bars with a message like: A RenderFlex overflowed by 24 pixels on the bottom or Vertical viewport was given unbounded height.

The Fix

Wrap the inner ListView in an Expanded widget, or set the ListView's property Shrink Wrap: True and Physics: NeverScrollableScrollPhysics if nested within a parent single-child scrollview.
